newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt TV maker public offering oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Egypt TV maker public offering oversubscribed.

text.p: The Egyptian state will give up a majority stake in Telemisr/Arab Transistor Radio and Electronics Supplies after an offer of 10 percent of the firm was more than 35 times oversubscribed, the agent for the sale said on Monday.
The state had originally offered 200,000 shares representing the 10 percent to private and institutional investors, but said it was willing to increase the shares if demand warrants.
"We've had a tremendous amount of orders and the state is considering selling a total 50 percent to individuals," said Mohammed el-Sharnoubi of Banque Misr.
Telemisr's workers own an additional 10 percent, which would reduce the state's holding in the firm to 40 percent.
Telemisr is the state's leading manufacturer of colour and black and white television sets, also producing sets under licence from Korean firm Goldstar and Japan's NEC Corp.
Its net after-tax profit for the 1995/96 financial year fell to 10.34 million pounds from 10.91 million a year earlier but net sales were higher 10.84 million at 180.88 million.
Successful shareholders will also receive a minimum 3.10 pound dividend per share for 1995/96.
